title: Armstrong's invitation at the Roosevelt Grill and his funeral
summary: Armstrong sits in with Peanuts Hucko's quartet and says he wants Leeman in his band, but Leeman could not leave New York; he watches the funeral on television.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Then when I was with the Peanuts Hucko Quartet at the Roosevelt Grill, Louis had been real sick towards the end, and he was recuperating. He came down with his wife, Lucille, to hear us. Peanuts had been with Louis for a long time -- he did some of those lengthy world wide trips with him. He made some movies with him, and that was a few years back, and Louis got up for nostalgia's sake, I couldn't believe it -- and he was a little bit weak, but he had that beautiful grin, and he came up on the bandstand and sang "Hello Dolly", "Blueberry Hill" and he did "Rocking Chair" and Peanuts sang with him, feeding in that Jack Teagarden, what Jack Teagarden did on that original record, he talked back and forth, and then he capped it all off with "Sleepy Time Down South".

Afterwards, he had Lou McGarity and Peanuts and myself over to his table and he said, "Lucille, by my judge and witness; when I reorganize and I get to feel better, I want these three boys in my band" -- and he says,
"You tell that to Joe Glaser for me".

Well, however, Louis never did recuperate enough to have that band; however, to this day, I'm so proud that he asked me. Joe Glaser called me to join Louis when I was on the Hit Parade -- I couldn't afford to leave New York with the work I was doing, I was always sorry later on in life.

I had a pass to the funeral when Louis passed away, and well, you couldn't get into the church without one. I was just too emotional to go, so I sat at home here only two and a half miles away from the church and watched it on television.
